purpose: Map existing standards and project mechanisms before changing intention, interpretation or need persistence.

sources.name: W3C ActivityStreams 2.0 / Activity Vocabulary
sources.warning: ActivityStreams audience/addressing semantics are not an authorization model and MUST NOT replace CZ access control.

sources.name: Schema.org WantAction
sources.finding: Useful precedent for expressing desire by an agent, but insufficient for provenance, interpretation, acceptance, revision and privacy.

sources.name: Schema.org Demand
sources.finding: Useful for public seeking of goods/services; too commercial and narrow to define CZ Need generally.

sources.name: Open311 GeoReport
sources.finding: Useful precedent for source/status lifecycle of requests, but domain-specific to civic service requests.

sources.name: AT Protocol Repository
sources.finding: Useful precedent for portable user repositories, record revisions and exports.
incompatibilities: Repository content is public by design.
Record deletion can leave no tombstone.
Current CZ semantic history requires explicit preservation of prior decisions while personal-data lifecycle may require selective redaction/deletion.

sources.name: Solid Web Access Control
sources.finding: Useful separation of read/write/append/control privileges and privacy considerations; CZ can preserve this property with PostgreSQL RLS and bounded capabilities.

sources.name: Data Privacy Vocabulary 2.3
sources.warning: DPV is vocabulary support for compliance metadata, not legal authority and not proof of compliance.

property_decisions.cz_semantics: Preserve the original human record as historical source material. Later interpretation, correction or withdrawal must not rewrite what was originally recorded.
Every intention or interpretation must identify the responsible Actor or producing mechanism.
An interpretation must point to the exact source record(s) it interpreted; derivation does not imply correctness.
A revised intention is a new record linked to the prior record, not an overwrite.
Withdrawal ends operational use without pretending the historical record never existed.
Acceptance or rejection is a separately attributable human direction about whether an interpretation may become operative; it is not truth verification.
Keep PostgreSQL RLS and bounded capabilities. Study WAC's separation of read/write/append/control; do not install a Solid runtime.
Represent purpose, processing, personal-data category/source, legal basis, recipients, storage/retention and rights where relevant. Vocabulary metadata does not itself establish legal compliance.
Schema.org Demand may be useful for a subset of public external serialization, but it must not define the general CZ Need model.

extension_candidates.concrete_property_lost_without_extension: The current project_intents record cannot reliably distinguish who or what produced an interpretation or reconstruct the exact source record used.

accepted_at and accepted_by are embedded in an append-only content record, so later human acceptance, rejection or withdrawal cannot be represented without conflating content creation with human direction.
projects.current_intent can drift from the accepted intention history and become an independent second source of truth.
projects.needs text[] cannot preserve attribution, source, acceptance, version, withdrawal or the distinction between a declared need and an inferred interpretation.

Free-text intentions and needs can contain personal or sensitive data; append-only semantic history alone cannot satisfy minimisation, correction, retention and applicable deletion/anonymisation duties.

deferred.reason: AI-derived needs remain Interpretation until explicit human acceptance; no current need for automatic extraction.
Discovery semantics are not yet mature enough to justify inference/ranking infrastructure.
Study semantics now; only build federation if a real interoperability requirement appears.
Must be revisited with WORLD-003 after publication, privacy and withdrawal semantics are implemented.

falsifiers: If existing append-only events can represent acceptance/rejection/withdrawal without a new decision table while preserving exact authority and reconciliation, prefer that smaller mechanism.
If needs prove to be only a projection of accepted intent for real workflows, do not create an independent Need entity.
If a more general interoperable Need standard is found that preserves attribution, lifecycle and non-commercial semantics, MAP it instead of defining CZ-specific semantics.
If public discovery works with explicit accepted records alone, do not introduce embeddings, inferred needs or ranking.
